reviewed_invariants: Application cleanup erases exactly the 8192-byte RAM backing and 4096-byte cache without touching the resident kernel or Editor metadata.
Every executable word is copied to RAM; only offsets below 4096 are copied to cache.
RAM tail copies advance only after a completed RAM write; source staging remains live through the final word.
Staged executable size still permits 8192 bytes, while larger programs take the existing recovery path.
Cache flush reads/writes only min(executable_bytes,4096), preserves direct-RAM tail contents, and reports bytes actually flushed.
The existing SoC address mux uses cache for CPU addresses below SHAMA_CACHE_BYTES and RAM for the tail.
Resource reports count the complete executable once in RAM and only its cached prefix in the separate fast-memory pool.

Full physical cache generation and saved-world execution remain separate acceptance gates.
